target_customer: Android consumers overwhelmed by lock screen notifications
problem: Android phones show an undifferentiated stream of notifications, so users miss important alerts.
business_model: Free consumer Android app with no stated revenue model
product_category: Android lock screen and notification manager

founders.name: Yin Wu
education: Stanford University, computer science (left in 2011 to join Y Combinator)
founders.background_notes: YC page says she is a three-time YC alumna (S11, S13, W20) and later sold a company to Microsoft in 2015, then was a principal engineer at Microsoft.

founders.name: Xuwen Cao
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; TechCrunch coverage names him as Prim co-founder.

exit.reason: Microsoft bought Double Labs, the company behind Echo; reports say the deal closed in August 2015 and was reported in September.

competitors.name: Cover
competitors.what: Contextual Android lock screen replacement that showed apps by context

technical_complexity.rationale: A notification filtering lock screen app is a single platform Android project; categorization logic adds modest difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Lock screens were easy to copy and Android and Microsoft's own app could replicate the feature.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Microsoft already had Next Lock Screen and bought Double Labs in 2015; Echo was later removed from the Play Store.

market_need_then: Notification overload on Android was a common complaint, though the YC S13 product started as the laundry startup Prim; Echo launched July 2014.

identity.visual_style: Minimal design that press said consumed less battery

branding.community_and_virality: Android press covered the app; Business Insider reported about 50,000 Play Store reviews in 2015.

brand_strength.rationale: The app had notable review volume and press, but the name was generic and there was no other brand asset.

pivots.to: Echo, Android lock screen notification app
pivots.why: Prim failed; the team turned to Echo, per TechCrunch coverage cited in search results.

outcome_analysis: Echo came from the team behind failed laundry startup Prim, launched in mid 2014 and grew to a popular Android lock screen with about 50,000 reviews. It was bought by Microsoft's Double Labs deal in 2015 for an undisclosed price and was later pulled from the Play Store, which reads as a talent and technology absorption rather than a standalone success, in a category that depended on Android and was easy to copy.
notes: No funding amounts found; Crunchbase and CB Insights show a seed led by Y Combinator with amounts hidden, so unknown is not zero. The directory says the company launched with the YC S13 batch as Prim, so the 2013 founded year refers to Prim. Pivot date July 2014 from search summary. Exact acquisition date: CB Insights says 2015-09-14; reports say the deal happened in August. Pre-2014 competitor sources are 2012 and 2013 era but not specific to Echo.
